title_en: Amanda Lynam, Chief Credit Strategist in Global Investment Research, Goldman Sachs
title_zh: Amanda Lynam（Goldman Sachs）：AI 发行周期下的信用市场
subtitle_zh: Goldman Sachs 信用策略主管 Amanda Lynam 谈超大规模云服务商 CAPEX 发债、利差格局与组合分散。
description: Amanda Lynam, Chief Credit Strategist in Global Investment Research, Goldman Sachs

turns.en: If you just look at the CAPEX figures from 2026 through 2030 for the group of hyperscalers, that CAPEX estimate is upwards of $6 trillion. So it is significant if you push that out through 2031.
turns.zh: 你只看 2026 到 2030 年这一组超大规模云服务商（hyperscalers）的资本开支（CAPEX）数字，那个 CAPEX 预估就已经超过 6 万亿美元。所以如果你把它推到 2031 年，规模是相当可观的。

turns.en: And then you also include what's already been invested in 2025. Those numbers are even larger. And of course, here I'm just focusing on the hyperscaler ecosystem.
turns.zh: 然后你再算上 2025 年已经投进去的那部分，数字还会更大。当然，我这里只是聚焦于超大规模云服务商这一个生态圈。

turns.en: But what we found in our work is that actually the hyperscalers are only 40% of total AI-related gross issuance. So the theme is actually much broader.
turns.zh: 但我们研究后发现，超大规模云服务商其实只占到 AI 相关总发行量的 40%，所以这个主题其实更宽。

turns.en: Hello, this is Dean Kernott. And welcome to the Alpha Exchange, where we explore topics in financial markets associated with managing risk, generating return, and the deployment of capital in the alternative investment industry.
turns.zh: 大家好，我是 Dean Kernott，欢迎收听 Alpha Exchange。在这个节目里，我们会探讨金融市场中的话题，涉及风险管理、收益创造，以及另类投资行业的资本部署。

turns.en: My guest today on the Alpha Exchange is Amanda Lynum. She is a chief credit strategist in global investment research at Goldman Sachs. Amanda, it's a pleasure to welcome you back to the podcast.
turns.zh: 我今天请到的嘉宾是 Amanda Lynam。她是 Goldman Sachs 全球投资研究的信用策略主管。Amanda，很高兴欢迎你再次回到这个播客。

turns.en: Thank you for having me back, Dean. It's great to see you. It was great to run into you recently at Bloomberg. And you're a person that I've wanted to talk to because there's so much going on in your area of expertise around credit and all of the things that you're doing.
turns.zh: 谢谢你请我回来，Dean，很高兴见到你。前几天在 Bloomberg 碰到你真开心，我一直想跟你聊聊，因为你专长的信用领域、以及你们在做的所有事情，实在有太多可聊的了。

turns.en: Credit and all of the CAPEX and AI build out. So we're going to have a lot to talk about. You were on the podcast. I just checked in October of 2023.
turns.zh: 信用、CAPEX、还有 AI 基础设施建设，我们今天有得聊了。你上次来这个播客我刚查了下，是在 2023 年 10 月。

turns.en: And it's probably the case. You'll know it better than I do. But perhaps free cash flow for the hyperscalers probably peak the next year, is my guess.
turns.zh: 大概是那样，你比我更清楚。我猜，超大规模云服务商的自由现金流（free cash flow）可能就在明年触顶。

turns.en: And it's kind of been on a one-way train lower as they issue so much debt. So we're going to talk a lot about that. So let's get the conversation going.
turns.zh: 因为它们发债发得太多，自由现金流其实一直在单边走低。我们今天就要多聊聊这块，那我们开始吧。

turns.en: Give us the big picture as you frame out the credit landscape, whether it's with respect to the supply side, the demand side. We can talk about credit fundamentals.
turns.zh: 在你把整个信用图景描绘出来时，先给我们一个大局观——不管是供给端还是需求端，我们都可以谈到信用的基本面。

turns.en: I'll just turn it to you just to give us the big picture. And then we can drill down into some of the specifics. Sure, that sounds great. So at a high level, I would say we're generally constructive on corporate credit due to a few fundamental factors.
turns.zh: 我把话头交给你，先给我们讲一个大局，然后再深入聊一些细节。好的，听起来不错。总的来说，我大概会讲，我们对公司信用整体是建设性的看法，原因有几项基本面因素。

turns.en: One is the macroeconomic backdrop is probably good enough for credit at this point. So anywhere around trend or even slightly above trend growth is a pretty favorable backdrop for corporate credit.
turns.zh: 一是宏观经济背景到目前为止对信用来说大概已经足够好了。所以只要增长处于趋势水平，甚至略高于趋势，对公司信用来讲都是相当有利的环境。

turns.en: And that's essentially what we have. And presumably, that is something that I think extends across a range of asset classes, but is definitely a supportive factor for credit.
turns.zh: 而这基本上也正是我们目前所拥有的。而且这个环境我想可以延伸到一系列资产类别，但对公司信用而言，它的确是一个支撑因素。

turns.en: Second on the fundamental side, we have pretty solid fundamental metrics. Our team has done a lot of work identifying dispersion under the surface.
turns.zh: 第二，在基本面层面，我们的基本面指标算相当扎实。我们团队做了很多工作，去识别表面之下的分化（dispersion）。

turns.en: But the fact remains is that whether you look at leverage or coverage, really, it's pretty solid from a fundamental credit perspective. So that's another really supportive anchor, fundamentally speaking, on credit.
turns.zh: 但事实仍然是：无论是看杠杆率还是利息保障倍数（coverage），从信用基本面的角度看，其实都相当稳固，这是另一个从基本面上看真正支撑信用的锚。

turns.en: And then the technicals have been what I would characterize as significantly supportive for credit, specifically the yield-based backdrop for US and European credit, specifically.
turns.zh: 然后是技术面，我认为可以用「显著支撑」来描述当前信用环境的技术面，具体来说就是美国和欧洲信用的收益率驱动（yield-based）背景。

turns.en: We've had a couple of years now of elevated all-in yields. And it's really brought in a wave of buying from a very large and powerful cohort, specifically yield-based investors like insurers, pensions, and even foreign demand, which has remained on pace actually to exceed 2025's full-year record.
turns.zh: 我们已经连续好几年处于较高的到期收益率（all-in yields），这吸引了一大批非常庞大且有实力的资金买入，具体来说就是那些看重收益率的投资者，比如保险公司、养老金，甚至海外需求，其节奏实际上有望超过 2025 年全年的纪录。

turns.en: So when you put those things together, kind of good enough growth from a macroeconomic perspective, solid fundamentals as it relates to the corporate borrowers in our market, albeit with some dispersion, and then a very powerful technical that is incentivized yield-based investors to deploy, it results in a backdrop where periods of spread widening have not only been elusive, but they've been short-lived.
turns.zh: 把这几件事放在一起——宏观上「足够好」的增长，公司借款人基本面的稳健（虽有分化），再加上一股非常强大、激励收益率导向投资者去部署的技术面力量——结果是利差走阔的窗口不仅稀缺，而且转瞬即逝。

turns.en: And that's something that a range of investors and allocators have been navigating, because while we often hear that there's a fair amount of capital on the sidelines to deploy, the opportunities to deploy that at widespread levels have been episodic.
turns.zh: 这也是很多投资者和资产配置者一直在应对的局面：虽然我们常听到「场外还有一大笔待部署的资金」，但真正能在利差明显走阔的时点把这些钱配置出去的机会其实是一波一波、时有时无的。

turns.en: Now, that is the backdrop. Our forecasts, however, do call for some modest spread widening, but I think it's important to frame that in the context of the overall historical pattern.
turns.zh: 好，这就是背景。至于我们的预测，确实预计会有一些温和的利差走阔，但我觉得把它放在整体的历史图景里去理解很重要。

turns.en: And even the modest widening that we expect is not at all wide by historical standards. So when I have to think about the risks to our view, having outlined what I just went through, the risks to our view are for modestly wider spreads.
turns.zh: 甚至我们预期的那点温和走阔，按历史标准来看，都远远算不上宽。所以当我不得不去想我们观点的风险时——在我刚讲的框架之外——风险就是利差会适度走阔一点。

turns.en: But again, we're still pretty constructive. I think the key message that I would highlight away from the immediate discussion on AI-related supply, the key risk that I would frame is that right now, the rate's backdrop has been a tailwind for credit.
turns.zh: 但话说回来，我们仍然相当建设性。我想跳出刚才关于 AI 相关供给的即时讨论，强调一个关键信息：当下利率背景对信用其实是一股顺风。

turns.en: And what we are watching closely is that, is there a tipping point where the rates volatility in the rates market increases such that rates become a headwind for credit?
turns.zh: 我们密切关注的，是利率市场会不会到达一个临界点——也就是利率波动率上升、利率反过来变成信用的逆风。

turns.en: We're not seeing that, but that's the one thing that I would put on my radar in terms of things to watch. And what is an otherwise constructive backdrop for credit?
turns.zh: 我们目前还没看到，但如果要说我的观察名单上有一件事，那就是这个。除此之外，什么才是一个对信用本来看起来建设性的背景？

turns.en: Let's go a little deeper on the corporate fundamentals. So as a lender, the best you can do is get your coupons and your money back. And so you're really concerned about the borrower's capacity to pay.
turns.zh: 我们把公司基本面再挖深一点。作为贷款人，你最好的结果就是拿回你的票息和本金，所以你真正担心的是借款人的偿付能力。

turns.en: Take us through from the way you look at things and maybe the macro assessment of that, whether it's leverage, free interest coverage, give us a sense as to where that is now.
turns.zh: 请你从你观察问题的方式出发——也许再带上宏观的评估——不管是杠杆、利息保障、还是净利息保障，给我们一个当下它们处在什么水平的感觉。

turns.en: And then maybe juxtapose it versus previous cycles, how safe does that look just from the lender's standpoint? I would say the widening that we are expecting in corporate credit spreads is really a function of technical indigestion of elevated supply and not necessarily a concern about deteriorating fundamentals, at least for the most part.
turns.zh: 然后再跟以往周期做个对比，单纯从贷款人的角度看，那有多安全？我会说，我们预期中的公司信用利差走阔，更多是技术面消化大量供给的结果，而不是对基本面恶化的担忧，至少大部分情况下是这样。

turns.en: Where I would call out the most risk from a fundamental perspective and where interest coverage metrics really warrant closer monitoring is in what we call the left tail of the credit market.
turns.zh: 如果要说我认为风险最集中、需要更密切监控利息保障指标的地方，那是在我们所说的信用市场的左尾（left tail）。

turns.en: So triple C's in US and European high yield or even certain subsets of the private credit market, specifically very small borrowers from vintages that were formed in ultra low interest rate environments.
turns.zh: 也就是美国和欧洲高收益的 CCC 级，甚至私人信贷里的某些子集，具体来说是在超低利率环境下成立的那些年份（vintage）里非常小的借款人。

turns.en: There you do have interest coverage metrics that are either hovering close to one for some borrowers, fixed charge coverage metrics that are maybe below one or you have a tail of the market that has yet to grow into its elevated debt capital structures even over the past few years with a backdrop of supportive growth, as I mentioned.
turns.zh: 在那儿，你确实会看到一些借款人的利息保障指标贴着 1 徘徊，固定费用保障指标可能低于 1，还有一批尾部市场在过去几年里，虽然有支持性的增长背景，但仍然没有长到能消化它们偏高的债务资本结构。

turns.en: Using the US IG market as an example, what you see is that credit metrics are still pretty solid interest coverage metrics in particular. So no one, at least in terms of our mainstream conversations with institutional investors, I should say very few investors are focused on a significant deterioration in credit metrics or an inability to be repaid for the broader subset of the market.
turns.zh: 拿美国投资级（IG）市场做例子，你会看到信用指标——尤其是利息保障——依然相当稳健。所以至少在我们跟机构投资者的主流交流里，几乎没有投资人真正关注信用指标大幅恶化，或者更大范围市场违约无法偿付的问题。

turns.en: You are seeing a fair amount of dispersion, however, in that left tail and I would say as it relates to the leverage finance market, we actually think we're past peak defaults for this cycle because there's been a fair amount of either distressed exchange activity or formal defaults that have occurred over the past few years.
turns.zh: 不过你确实能看到左尾里存在相当的分化。而说到杠杆融资（leverage finance）市场，我们其实认为本周期的违约已经过了顶峰，因为过去几年已经出现了相当多的困境债务置换（distressed exchange）或者正式违约。

turns.en: Really what it is at the moment is a lagging of the overall resilient backdrop that we've seen across the corporate credit market. The one area that I do think as it relates to the fundamental discussion that is important to note is that we've almost shifted how we think about quality and defensiveness in the corporate credit market in this current backdrop relative to several years ago.
turns.zh: 眼下的局面，更像是整个公司信用市场富有韧性这一背景的一个滞后反映。而关于基本面讨论，我确实认为有一点值得注意：与几年前相比，在当前这个背景下，我们对公司信用市场里「质量」和「防御性」的定义，思路已经几乎发生了转变。

turns.en: And what I mean by that is historically, if you were to adopt say a more defensive posture or you wanted to move up in quality in the corporate credit market, that would generally map to moving higher in ratings.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，历史经验是：如果你想采取更防御的立场，或者想在信用市场里向更高质量迁移，那通常就对应着往评级上端走。

turns.en: And one of the points that we've made recently in our research is that if you do that in IG and high yield, so if you move into the higher end of the rating spectrum in each of those respective markets, so that would be double A's and IG and double B's and high yield, what you are doing is encountering in many instances a more pronounced headwind on two fronts.
turns.zh: 我们最近研究里提到的一个观点是，如果你真在 IG 或高收益里这样做——也就是往各自市场评级谱系的高端去，比如 IG 里的 AA、高收益里的 BB——很多情况下你反而会在两条战线上碰到更明显的逆风。

turns.en: One, that's where a lot of the supply has been concentrated. So a lot of the tech related supply has been at the high end of the IG rating spectrum.
turns.zh: 第一，那正是很多供给集中的地方。大量的科技相关发行集中在 IG 评级谱系的高端。

turns.en: And even in high yield, a lot of the project finance issuance for data centers in particular has been double B rated. So you have a bit of a more pronounced supply headwind at the high end.
turns.zh: 甚至在高收益里，很多数据中心项目融资（project finance）的发行也都是 BB 级。所以高端市场承受了更明显的供给逆风。

turns.en: And then what you also have is a bit of a more duration exposure in those pockets of the market. So as you move up in rating, you have a thinner spread cushion to buffer your total returns from the elevated level of global bond yields that I referenced earlier.
turns.zh: 另外，那些角落里的市场久期也偏长一点。所以当你往评级上端走，你的利差缓冲就更薄，越难抵消我前面提到的偏高全球债券收益率对总回报的冲击。

turns.en: So it's pretty interesting that in our view, the more attractive relative value posturing that we see is to selectively move down in credit quality.
turns.zh: 所以很有意思的一点是，站在我们的角度看，更具吸引力的相对价值姿态，其实是选择性地往信用质量下端走。

turns.en: And that may sound a little counterintuitive given the tight level of spreads. But again, the spreads are tight for, in many cases, pretty good reasons.
turns.zh: 在利差这么紧的情况下，这话听起来可能有点反直觉。但利差之所以紧，在很多情况下恰恰是有相当合理原因的。

turns.en: And what defines quality and defensiveness in this market, I think warrants a reevaluation. And so for IG in particular, that leaves us overweight triple Bs versus the higher end of the rating spectrum in US high yield.
turns.zh: 我反而觉得，在这个市场里，什么才算「质量」和「防御性」，本身就应该被重新审视。具体到 IG，这让我们选择超配 BBB，相对更高端的评级区间；在美国高收益，

turns.en: That leaves us overweight single Bs relative to double Bs, for example, very selective in that triple C cohort. So less about the fundamental metrics.
turns.zh: 让我们超配 B 级、相对 BB 级，并对 CCC 那一档做非常精挑细选。所以重点不在于基本面指标——

turns.en: In most cases, they're still pretty solid, but more about what does actually quality and defensiveness mean in this market and how is that different from even several years ago?
turns.zh: 大多数情况下它们依然挺稳，重点是「质量」和「防御性」在这个市场里到底意味着什么，以及跟几年前有什么不同。

turns.en: I definitely want to circle back to the big picture of portfolio construction. I know we talked about areas like pharma as just different. Perhaps it's banks as well.
turns.zh: 我特别想回到组合构建的大画面。我记得我们聊过像 pharma 这样不一样的领域，也许银行也是。

turns.en: I think you mentioned food and beverage. So I want to circle back to that. As you were describing this search for value and maybe avoiding some areas of concentration, I just couldn't help but think about the S&P tracker, of which there is just an enormous amount of passive capital tracking the S&P, which they say passive investing is an active decision.
turns.zh: 你好像提到食品饮料。所以我想回过头再聊聊这个话题。当你讲到那种寻找价值、避开一些集中度领域的时候，我忍不住想到标普 500 指数追踪（S&P tracker）——追踪标普的被动资金规模巨大，有人说被动投资其实本身就是一种主动决定。

turns.en: You wind up with this very, very concentrated, if passive portfolio where the top 10 stocks are 40%, they're all mega cap tech. I'm curious if you can maybe describe what's happening for the index aware investor in credit and how that looks in terms of the migration of exposures that's come as a result of this enormous capex build out.
turns.zh: 结果你就有了一个极度集中的被动组合，前十大股票占到 40%，全都是超大盘科技。我很好奇，你能不能描述一下，对于关注指数的信用投资者来说，正在发生什么？在这场巨大的 CAPEX 建设之下，敞口结构（exposure）发生了怎样的迁移？

turns.en: How has the index hugger, how has that portfolio changed relative to the last time you were on in 2023 before this giant capex trade really started to expand?
turns.zh: 那些贴着指数走（index hugger）的投资者，他们的组合相对你 2023 年最后一次上节目、当时这轮巨大的 CAPEX 交易还没真正展开时，发生了怎样的变化？

turns.en: It's a great question, Dean. So let's use USIG perhaps as the most relevant proxy to this wave of supply. So in the USIG bond market, let's use the Bloomberg index.
turns.zh: 好问题，Dean。那我们用 USIG 来做这一波供给的最贴切代理吧。在 USIG 债券市场里，我们用 Bloomberg 指数来看。

turns.en: Tech as a sector is around 10% of that index approximately. If you add some of the AI related names that are not classified as tech, what our work has suggested is that AI related exposure as a percentage of notional.
turns.zh: 科技作为一个板块，大约占这个指数 10% 左右。如果你再把一些并不被归为科技的 AI 相关名字加进来，我们研究给出的数字是：AI 相关敞口，按名义本金算——

turns.en: And again, I'm just focusing on index eligible debt here is around 12%. So it's meaningful. It's definitely increased relative to the past few years as the pace of supply from what have historically been cash rich sectors has increased.
turns.zh: 我这里说的都还是指可纳入指数的债务——大约占 12%。这是有意义的，相对过去几年确实在上升，因为历史上那些现金充裕板块的发行节奏在加快。

turns.en: But it's actually not yet the largest sector in the USIG market. That title firmly remains with US banks and actually the global banking sector in general, which is around 21, 22% of that same index.
turns.zh: 但它其实还并不是 USIG 里最大的板块，这个头衔依然稳稳属于美国银行，乃至全球银行业，占同一个指数大约 21%、22%。

turns.en: Focusing on index eligible debt is a little bit imperfect. We should add the caveat because there has been a wave of project finance issuance to fund data centers and chip financings, which are private.
turns.zh: 只盯着可指数化的债务，是有点不完美的，这里要加个说明。因为为数据中心和芯片融资而发行的项目融资债有一大批是私募的。

turns.en: We call them 144A for life. So they're not index eligible in IG, but the pattern is still pretty clear is that this is a growing sector. It's a meaningful sector, but it's not yet the largest sector.
turns.zh: 我们叫它们 144A for life，所以它们不能进入 IG 指数，但模式依然很清楚：这是一个在成长的板块，是一个有分量的板块，但还不是最大的板块。

turns.en: Now, the path forward, I think this is a really interesting point because when you talk to a range of asset allocators, it really depends on their perspective and their lens about how comfortable they are taking outsized exposure to any given name or theme.
turns.zh: 至于未来路径——我觉得这一点特别有意思，因为当你跟各种资产配置者聊，他们对承担任何单一名字或主题的超大规模敞口有多大舒适区，取决于他们的视角和观察角度。

turns.en: In the equity market, our colleagues there, they share in the upside of equity market momentum. And so what you found is that the equity market can be more comfortable running larger exposures to any given theme or issuer because they are sharing in the upside.
turns.zh: 在股票市场，我们的股票同事能分享股票市场动量上涨的红利，所以你会发现股票市场可以更坦然地承担对某个主题或某个发行人更大的敞口，因为它们也在分享上涨。

turns.en: As you correctly noted in credit, we tend to focus more on the downside. We're just hoping to get paid back at maturity at par. And so it's a bit of a different calculus.
turns.zh: 而在信用市场，正如你恰当地指出的，我们更关心下行。我们只希望能到期按面值拿回本金。所以这是一套不同的算法。

turns.en: And I would offer a higher hurdle to justify very large exposures to any given name or theme that does not mean that it's not possible. It's certainly possible.
turns.zh: 我会给出一个更高的门槛，才能证明对某个名字或主题非常大的敞口合理。这并不意味着不可能，当然可能。

turns.en: And of course, again, the banking sector is a great example of that in how large some of those sector exposures can be. But I would say it is a little bit different.
turns.zh: 银行业就是很好的例子，说明某些板块敞口可以做到多大。但我想说，多少是不同的。

turns.en: The path of travel in our view over time is that very simply as this multi-year AI issuance cycle extends, we see scope for the US IG bond market in particular to do a lot more of the heavy lifting in 2027 and 2028 because there's still a bit of a runway for these names and hyperscalers and otherwise to issue before they start becoming the largest issuers in the market.
turns.zh: 在我们看来，未来随着这一轮多年 AI 发行周期延续，路径其实很简单：美国 IG 债券市场在 2027 和 2028 年会承担更多的重担，因为这一批名字、这些超大规模云服务商、以及其他发行人，还有相当一段时间可以发行，才会开始成为市场里最大的发行群体。

turns.en: After that, we expect a more nuanced conversation, so call it 2028 and beyond, about where exactly to take this risk as an allocator and at what price.
turns.zh: 在那之后，我们预计会迎来一场更细致的讨论——大致是 2028 年以后——关于作为配置者究竟该在哪儿承担这个风险、以什么价格承担。

turns.en: And we expect in those later years of this AI issuance build out to see the private markets in particular to do more of the heavy lifting there.
turns.zh: 我们也预计，在这轮 AI 发行建设的后期年份里，私募市场（private markets）会承担更重的担子。

turns.en: Again, because we do think that the binding constraint in this financing cycle is more likely to lie in the context of what the market conventions are in terms of issuer concentration to a given name or theme and less about how much debt could these firms issue and stay comfortably within IG territory because that second calculus, the figure of how much they can issue and stay in IG territory is probably factors larger
turns.zh: 再次强调，因为在这轮融资周期里，真正的紧约束，更可能落在「市场惯例对单一名或单一主题的集中度上限是多少」上，而不是「这些公司能发多少债、还能稳在 IG 之内」——因为后者那个尺度，也就是它们能发多少而留在 IG，大概是前者的若干倍级差距，

turns.en: than what we assume can be placed in the US IG bond market alone. So I would say it's important to note that we're not concerned at all actually about access to capital for this theme because we talk to a wide range of investors that are eager and excited about participating.
turns.zh: 比我们能假设可以被美国 IG 债券市场单独消化的规模要大得多。所以我想说，值得注意的一点是：我们其实完全不担心这个主题的资本可得性，因为我们接触的一大批投资者都热情高涨，愿意参与。

turns.en: But the nuance here is that we just don't expect the US IG bond market to do the entirety of the heavy lifting in the financing for multiple years to come because we do expect that investors will be a bit more nuanced about issuer concentration and market saturation.
turns.zh: 但微妙之处在于：我们并不指望美国 IG 债券市场在未来多年里独自挑起全部的融资重担，因为投资者会对单名集中度和市场饱和更挑剔一些。

turns.en: Give us a little bit of context as someone who's been looking at this stuff for decades and has seen lots of different cycles. Give us a sense of the scope of the hyperscaler build out in terms of debt issuance and using it for capex.
turns.zh: 作为一个研究这个话题几十年、看过很多不同周期的人，请给我们一些背景，讲一讲超大规模云服务商这一轮建设在债务发行、以及用它来做 CAPEX 方面的规模感。

turns.en: The estimates I think as many market participants are aware of have continued to move higher over time. So there's been an upward drift. But as it stands right now, using our colleagues in GIR equity research, if you just look at the capex figures from 2026 through 2030 for the group of hyperscalers, that capex estimate is upwards of $6 trillion.
turns.zh: 我想很多市场参与者也都注意到了，相关预估一直在往上抬，存在一种上偏。但按目前的口径——引用我们 GIR 股票研究同事的数据——只看 2026 到 2030 年这一组超大规模云服务商的 CAPEX 数字，那个预估就已经超过 6 万亿美元。

turns.en: So it is significant if you push that out through 2031 and then you also include what's already been invested in 2025, those numbers are even larger.
turns.zh: 所以如果你把它推到 2031 年，再算上 2025 年已经投入的那部分，数字还会更大。

turns.en: And of course, here I'm just focusing on the hyperscaler ecosystem. But what we found in our work is that actually the hyperscalers are only 40% of total AI related gross issuance.
turns.zh: 当然，我这里只是聚焦于超大规模云服务商这一个生态圈。但我们研究后发现，超大规模云服务商其实只占到 AI 相关总发行量的 40%。

turns.en: So the theme is actually much broader than that. The way that we've thought about the role of the debt markets really factors into this takeaway in our view that these companies are proactively getting ahead of fundraising to invest in this theme over a multi-year cycle.
turns.zh: 所以这个主题其实比那更宽。我们理解债务市场所扮演角色的方式，其实内嵌在我们研究里的一个结论中：这些公司是在多年周期里，主动提前做融资，为投入这个主题做准备。

turns.en: So actually when we first approached outlining forecasts for this effort, what we initially thought we were going to do was to take a look at the cashflow from operations from the hyperscalers and the capex and take the difference between the two and use that as a financing delta or gap that would have needed to be serviced in the debt markets.
turns.zh: 其实当我们刚开始为这项努力做预估的时候，我们原本打算做的是：看这些超大规模云服务商的经营活动现金流（cash flow from operations）和 CAPEX，把两者差额作为需要在债务市场里融资填补的资金缺口（financing delta）。

turns.en: And what we quickly realized when we did that is that that's probably not the right approach because if you did that approach, what you would have concluded is that there was not a need to raise debt in 2025 and that there was barely a need to raise debt in 2026 because until recently, as you noted at the start, cash flow from operations was either in excess of capex or close to it.
turns.zh: 但我们很快发现，那种做法大概不合适，因为如果你真那么算，你会得出 2025 年根本不需要发债，2026 年也几乎不需要发债——因为正如你在节目开头指出的，经营活动现金流此前一直超过 CAPEX 或接近 CAPEX。

turns.en: What instead we saw on the ground in kind of reality is that the hyperscalers globally issued 108 billion of global IG debt in 2025. And so far this year, so we're recording this in mid-September, they've issued 229 billion of global investment grade debt.
turns.zh: 而我们在现场看到的真实情况是：这些超大规模云服务商在 2025 年全球发行了 1080 亿美元的全球投资级债，而今年到目前为止——我们是 9 月中旬录制的这期——他们已经发行了 2290 亿美元的全球投资级债。

turns.en: So that's the path of travel that we see is that a pretty meaningful size issuance from the hyperscalers in 2025, at least relative to the pattern of the prior decade plus where they weren't really active issuers in the debt markets.
turns.zh: 所以我们看到的路径是：2025 年超大规模云服务商的发行规模相对过去十多年已经相当有意义，此前它们并不是债务市场里的活跃发行人。

turns.en: And then a pretty meaningful increase so far in 2026 for the full year, we're expecting 250 billion of hyperscaler global supply. And then we actually expect a 60% increase in 2027 where we're penciling in 400 billion of global hyperscaler direct debt issuance.
turns.zh: 然后到 2026 年到目前为止也有相当明显的增长，全年我们预计超大规模云服务商全球供给达到 2500 亿美元。再往后，2027 年我们预计会增长 60%，把 4000 亿美元的超大规模云服务商直接债务发行计入我们的预测。

turns.en: And again here, I'm just thinking about the debt issuance from the hyperscalers and I am not capturing data center financing or chip financing.
turns.zh: 我这里说的还只是超大规模云服务商自身的债务发行，没有把数据中心融资或芯片融资算进来。

turns.en: We forecast that separately and that's another 300 billion for those keeping track in 2027. So these numbers are large, they're growing. They represent, in our view, getting ahead of a multi-year anticipated investment cycle.
turns.zh: 那些我们另外单独做预测，2027 年再加 3000 亿美元，供有兴趣的朋友合计。所以这些数字很庞大，还在增长，在我们看来体现的是「提前为一个多年投资周期做准备」。

turns.en: And really the way that we've landed on these forecasts is to make an assumption on the share of CAPEX that is debt financed. And that share we expect to peak in 2027 at 35%.
turns.zh: 我们之所以落到这些预测上，是做了一个 CAPEX 中债务融资占比的假设。这个比例我们预计会在 2027 年见顶，达到 35%。

turns.en: And that really just reflects the fact that there is a delay between AI investment and monetization of anywhere from three months to two years and we're incorporating that into our forecast.
turns.zh: 这背后的事实就是，AI 投资和 AI 变现之间有三到二十四个月的时滞，我们把这个因素计入了预测。

turns.en: I would say in our view though, that doesn't mean that the pace of issuance will slow in the outer years because again, if you just look at the forward estimates from our equity colleagues, CAPEX is still pretty abundant even in the later years.
turns.zh: 不过我认为，这并不意味着发行节奏在更远的年份会放缓，因为如果你只看股票同事给出的前瞻预估，CAPEX 即使在较晚年份也仍然相当充裕。

turns.en: And it will just be a function of market receptivity and investor sentiment on where exactly this debt gets placed. But it's important to note that we're really not concerned about access to capital because I think there are a wide range of pools of capital that are eager to participate here.
turns.zh: 剩下的只是市场接受度和投资者情绪决定这些债务究竟被配置到哪里。但值得注意的是，我们其实并不担心资本可得性，因为我觉得有各种各样的资金池都渴望参与其中。

turns.en: These are pretty enormous forward-looking CAPEX goals and debt issuance estimates. Would you say that's correct? I think it's large, but I also think it's important to think about the paradigm shift of where we are in overall US IG supply.
turns.zh: 这些前瞻 CAPEX 目标和债务发行预估都极其庞大，你会这样描述吗？我觉得是很大，但我也认为需要看清整个美国 IG 供给格局已经发生范式转变。

turns.en: So for example, our team just raised our US IG gross issuance forecast for 2026 across all sectors to 2.3 trillion. We were at 2.1 trillion and had been flagging upside risks to that view since June, but we were hesitant to formally raise it until recently because we anticipated a summer slowdown that never materialized.
turns.zh: 举个例子，我们团队刚刚把 2026 年跨全板块的美国 IG 毛发行量预测上调到 2.3 万亿。此前是 2.1 万亿，从 6 月起我们一直在提示上行风险，但迟迟没有正式上调，因为我们预期会有夏季放缓——但那并没有出现。

turns.en: And so now we've penciled in 2.3 trillion. If you compare that to the pandemic era boom, that would be a new record, of course, if you don't adjust for inflation.
turns.zh: 所以我们现在把 2.3 万亿写进预测。如果跟疫情时期的发行高峰相比，在不调整通胀的情况下，那将是一个新的历史纪录。

turns.en: So these are sizable run rates of the broader US IG market. And for 2027, we're actually penciling in 2.4 trillion of overall US IG gross issuance.
turns.zh: 也就是说，这些是整个美国 IG 市场相当大的运行水平。到 2027 年，我们预计美国 IG 毛发行总量为 2.4 万亿。

turns.en: So 400 billion direct from the hyperscaler sounds large. It is large. I mean, it is meaningful. It's an increase from the runway of the past few years.
turns.zh: 所以 4000 亿美元直接来自超大规模云服务商听起来大，也确实大，也是有分量的，相对过去几年的发行节奏是明显的抬升。

turns.en: And it will bump up their share of the overall indices, but they're starting from a low level of debt. And this is happening in the context of a very robust capital market cycle, AI and otherwise.
turns.zh: 它们会把这些名字在整体指数里的份额往上推，但它们是从一个较低的债务起点出发的。而且这一切发生在一个非常活跃的资本市场周期里，AI 和非 AI 都很活跃。

turns.en: One of the areas that's become a topic of conversation is this notion of a crowding out effect where 6% money for meta, that could be cheap for meta or a hyperscaler chasing what could be just an enormous right tail outcome for the equity perspective.
turns.zh: 其中一个热门话题是「挤出效应」（crowding out）——比如 Meta 用 6% 的资金成本发债，从 Meta 或一家超大规模云服务商的角度看，如果它追的是股票上那条可能极其肥厚的右尾，那 6% 也许并不算贵。

turns.en: And so those capital demands, I'm curious where you come out on this or where your colleagues and you come out on this, are those potential demands for capital from the hyperscalers?
turns.zh: 所以这些资本需求——我很好奇你的判断，你和你的同事怎么看——这些来自超大规模云服务商的潜在资本需求，

turns.en: Do they have the potential to crowd out, whether it's the US government or other firms that just don't get to enjoy the prospect of such a far right tail?
turns.zh: 会不会对美国政府或其他公司造成挤出，让那些不像超大规模云服务商那样享有遥远右尾前景的发行主体被排到一边？

turns.en: I can't imagine an industrial company in the US sees the capital as cheap as meta might see it now. How do you think about the unevenness of how the hyperscalers might see the costs of that capital versus whether it's the man in the street taking a mortgage or an industrial company in the US?
turns.zh: 我很难想象一家美国工业企业会像现在的 Meta 那样觉得资本便宜。你怎么看这种资本成本感知上的不均——超大规模云服务商眼里的资本成本，跟普通老百姓办房贷、跟一家美国工业企业的视角，差别在哪里？

turns.en: We actually see very little evidence of a crowding out as it relates to the hyperscaler issuance. Our rates colleagues have previously flagged that some of the upward momentum on US treasury yields, for example, may actually be more closely linked to the commodity market moves as opposed to hyperscaler supply.
turns.zh: 实际上，在超大规模云服务商发行的部分，我们几乎没有看到任何挤出效应的证据。我们的利率同事此前也提示过，美国国债收益率的一些上行势头，其推动力其实更可能与大宗商品市场的走势相关，而不是超大规模云服务商的供给。

turns.en: Of course, those in the credit market know that in periods of heavy gross issuance, there is some mechanical pressure on the rates market because a subset of investors will hedge interest rate risk.
turns.zh: 当然，信用市场里的人都知道，在毛发行量非常高的阶段，利率市场确实会承受一些机械压力，因为有一部分投资者会对冲利率风险。

turns.en: So just very mechanically, this is not related to AI supply, but just in general, if I'm an investor and I'm buying a 30 year new issue of any sort of corporate new deal and I'm wishing to hedge that interest rate risk, what I would do is sell treasuries on the other side in some sort of size, maybe match or maybe just partially.
turns.zh: 所以纯粹是机械层面的——这与 AI 供给无关。就拿一般情况说：如果我是投资者，买了一份 30 年期新发行的任何公司新券，又希望对冲利率风险，那我会在另一边以某种规模卖出国债——可能是大致匹配的对冲，也可能只是部分对冲。

turns.en: So there is a mechanical impact of periods of heavy gross new issuance in the corporate credit market. Do have some impact on the rates market, but very rarely would I attribute it to a crowding out from an asset allocation perspective.
turns.zh: 所以公司信用市场高毛发行阶段的的确确有机械影响，会对利率市场造成一些压力，但我很少会从资产配置的角度把它归因于挤出。

turns.en: I would more just attribute it to a mechanical impact from a hedging perspective. The other really interesting thing that we are observing from our seat is that the rest of the broader IG market is holding in really well.
turns.zh: 我更愿意把它归因于对冲角度下的机械影响。我们从我们这把椅子上观察到的另一件很有意思的事是：更广泛 IG 市场里其他部分真的相当稳。

turns.en: And you alluded to this at the start when we were talking about the overall view on credit. But if you look at IG index level spreads in IG, in aggregate, they've been pretty contained.
turns.zh: 你在开头谈整体信用观点时已经暗示过这一点。但你看 IG 指数层面的利差——整体而言——一直相当收敛。

turns.en: And if you look under the surface as we have done in our work and mapped AI related spread moves versus the broader market, so everything that is non-AI, what you see is that while the non-AI spreads in many instances are widening a little bit, it's very contained relative to the move that you see in the AI related ecosystem.
turns.zh: 而当我们像我们研究里那样，把表层之下的东西挖开——把 AI 相关利差走势跟更广泛的市场做映射，也就是所有非 AI 的部分——你会发现：尽管很多情况下非 AI 利差有轻微走阔，但相对 AI 生态圈里那种走阔幅度，还是相当收敛。

turns.en: And even the moves in the AI related ecosystem themselves are episodic periods of widening around supply indigestion. Again, importantly, it's not because investors are concerned for a significant fundamental deterioration because just the starting point is so strong.
turns.zh: 甚至 AI 相关生态圈的走阔本身，也是围绕供给消化出现的、一波一波、短暂的。重要的是，这并非投资者担心基本面显著恶化，因为起点本来就非常强。

turns.en: The implication, Dean, in that regard is that as it relates to the other sector, so whether that's banks, definitely energy has been well-bid because it's almost like a geopolitical hedge, healthcare, food and beverage.
turns.zh: 所以其中的含义就是，Dean，关于其他板块——不管是银行，能源显然被抢着买，几乎成了一种地缘政治对冲，还有医疗、食品饮料——

turns.en: These are sectors that I actually feel are benefiting from a diversification value from investors. And it's almost as though the sector diversification that those groups provide is almost even more precious to asset allocators because there's an expectation that again, the AI related acceleration and debt issuance is going to be a multi-year event.
turns.zh: 我实际觉得这些板块正在从投资者的分散配置价值里受益。简直就好像这些板块所提供的行业分散性，对资产配置者来说反而更加珍贵，因为大家预期，同样地，AI 相关的加速和债务发行将是一件持续多年的事情。

turns.en: AI related exposure in the credit market does look poised to grow. And so therefore, the sectors that you can get to diversify away from that, from a risk management perspective, that's a really important point.
turns.zh: AI 相关敞口在信用市场里看起来注定继续增长，因此，那些能让你分散开、避开它的板块，从风险管理角度来看就是一个非常重要的点。

turns.en: We also hear anecdotally from investors that there's an expectation that some of these sectors just might benefit from an overall technological improvement as it relates to AI.
turns.zh: 我们也从投资者那里听到一些传闻性的观察，认为其中一些板块也许整体上会从 AI 带来的技术改进中受益。

turns.en: So drug discovery and healthcare and pharma, we're all hopeful for that, but maybe that would improve the ability to develop drugs to meet some of these areas of high unmet medical need like cancer, for example.
turns.zh: 比如药物发现、医疗健康、制药——我们都为此抱有期待——也许 AI 会提升开发药物的能力，去满足像癌症这类高度未被满足的医疗需求。

turns.en: So there's a focus of credit investors, I think in keeping exposure to sectors that give them broader industry diversification. And I think that's what's allowing the credit market to hold in well.
turns.zh: 所以信用投资者会更倾向于保有那些能给他们更大行业分散的板块，我觉得这正是让信用市场能如此稳固的原因。

turns.en: So I don't sense that there's a crowding out. Maybe what it does, if I extrapolate this forward, is it may cause market participants and investors to kind of pick their spots earlier than you might expect.
turns.zh: 我没有感觉到有真正的挤出。如果我往前推演，也许它会带来的效果是，让市场参与者和投资者比大家预期的更早去择优布局。

turns.en: So for an allocator that's allocating across assets, maybe they have AI exposure in the common equity market, in converts, in private markets, in syndicated credit across regions, what they may think is that, okay, there's a broad set of AI related exposures coming in the credit market.
turns.zh: 对于一个跨资产做配置的投资者来说，可能他在普通股、可转债、私募市场、跨地区的银团信贷里都已经有 AI 敞口，他也许会想：好，信用市场里马上会涌来一大批 AI 相关敞口。

turns.en: When I pair that across all the asset classes that I own, how much exposure to the AI theme do I really want across all these asset classes?
turns.zh: 那么当我把它跟我持有的所有资产类别放在一起，我到底想在这些类别里合计承担多少 AI 主题敞口？

turns.en: And so therefore, might I be more selective in the asset classes like credit, for example? Do you get the sense that in this concept of the AI factor, there's been some discussion around, you've got to be careful that your portfolio may nominally look pretty diversified, but AI as a factor can kind of sneak in to certain exposures that don't look like AI, but might be AI, could be utilities that are selling power.
turns.zh: 因此，我是不是应该在信用这类资产里更精挑细选一些？你有没有感觉到，在所谓 AI 因子这个概念里——已经有些讨论——你要小心，你的组合名义上可能看起来很分散，但 AI 作为一个因子会悄悄溜进某些看起来不像 AI、却可能跟 AI 相关的敞口，比如那些卖电的公用事业（utilities）。

turns.en: EM can kind of look different, but it's got a heavy weighting, just given the exposure to memory in South Korea and so forth. Is that with respect to portfolio construction and this effort to diversify, is there a common discussion around trying to make sure you're not too AI centric, but don't realize it?
turns.zh: 新兴市场（EM）看起来是另一回事，但光是韩国存储（memory）敞口等因素，就让它的权重很重。就组合构建和分散化这件事而言，是不是有这样一个常见讨论：要确保你不至于以太以 AI 为中心的方式暴露，而自己却没意识到？

turns.en: Yeah, that's a great point. We factor that in actually, when we run our universe of firms that we believe are AI related, and therefore that's what generates our screen of AI related debt issuance.
turns.zh: 是的，这点很好。实际上我们在构建我们认为是 AI 相关的公司全集时，就已经把这个因素纳入了考虑——这也正是我们那份 AI 相关债务发行筛选的由来。

turns.en: For example, we leverage a wide variety of AI related baskets that have been developed by our colleagues in global banking and markets on the equity side.
turns.zh: 举例来说，我们会借助全球银行与市场（global banking and markets）部门同事在股票端开发的各种 AI 相关篮子（baskets）。

turns.en: We add to that names that we know are purely credit issuers, so they don't have public equity, but we know they're AI related, and that's how we come up with a broad universe of firms that we track for the AI related debt issuance that we publish every so often.
turns.zh: 我们再叠加进去我们知道纯做信用发行的名字——它们没有上市股票，但我们知道它们 AI 相关——我们就是这样得出一个宽口径的公司池，用来跟踪我们时不时发布的 AI 相关债务发行。

turns.en: As it relates to areas like utilities and machinery, we do take 30% of the issuance from those kind of AI tangential sectors as we refer to them, and we assume that's AI related.
turns.zh: 至于像公用事业和机械这类领域，我们实际上把这类我们所说的 AI 边缘行业（AI tangential sectors）发行额的 30% 计入，假设它们与 AI 相关。

turns.en: We acknowledge that for utilities issuance in particular, there are a lot of competing uses for that capital, just as one example, given the age of the infrastructure in the United States, we don't assume that 100% of that debt issuance is AI related, but we do assume that 30% of it is.
turns.zh: 我们承认，特别是公用事业发行，这笔资本有很多相互竞争的用途，仅举一例：鉴于美国基础设施的老化程度，我们并不假设这类债务发行 100% 都是 AI 相关，但我们确实假设其中 30% 是。

turns.en: So that is captured in our broader metrics. I will say, though, it's not the lion's share of the AI related issuance. If you look at the biggest contributors to AI related supply that we are tracking, it's first and foremost the hyperscalers, which are 40%, and then the other category that's large is the project finance issuers, so data center financing, GPU financing, let's call it another 22, 24%,
turns.zh: 所以这一点已经反映在我们更宽口径的指标里。不过我要说，它并不是 AI 相关发行里最大的一块。如果你看我们跟踪的 AI 相关供给里最大的贡献者，首当其冲是超大规模云服务商，占 40%；然后另一个大头是项目融资发行人——数据中心融资、GPU 融资——姑且算再占 22%、24%，

turns.en: and then you've got a broad range of issuers that are not hyperscalers, they're not project finance, but they're very clearly either in the tech or tech adjacent sectors that are meaningful, so software services, memory, PCs, equipment, things like that.
turns.zh: 然后是一大批既不是超大规模云服务商、也不是项目融资，但明显处在科技或科技相关领域、颇具分量的发行人，比如软件与服务、存储、PC、设备这类。

turns.en: That's the other big chunk of the AI related supply. Importantly, this is not just an IG phenomenon either, to your point, that high yield and leveraged loans have also had meaningful amounts of AI related issuance so far this year, and we also see it across regions.
turns.zh: 这是 AI 相关供给里另一个大块。重要的是，正如你所说，这不只是 IG 现象：今年到目前为止，高收益和杠杆贷款里也有相当多的 AI 相关发行，而且我们在各个地区都看得到。

turns.en: It's not even just a US capital markets phenomenon, and that's probably one of the disconnects that we expect to shift over the next, call it three months in 2026 and into 2027, is an accelerated share of AI related supply that is generated in the European credit markets, because so far they've almost under contributed relative to a range of other markets in terms of generating AI issuance, and given their size, especially relative
turns.zh: 这甚至不只是美国资本市场的现象。我们认为可能会发生转变的一个错配，大致在未来——姑且说 2026 年那三个月、并延续到 2027 年——就是在欧洲信用市场里生成的 AI 相关供给份额会加速增长，因为到目前为止，跟其他一系列市场相比，欧洲市场在生成 AI 发行方面几乎是贡献不足的；而考虑到它的规模，尤其相对

turns.en: to some of these really small regional corporate credit markets like Sterling and Swiss Frank and Canadian Dollar, we think that the European market is poised to generate more supply.
turns.zh: 英镑、瑞士法郎、加元这些真正很小的区域性公司信用市场而言，我们认为欧洲市场有能力生成更多供给。

turns.en: So you present this case for a lot of supply, but clearly the, we'll just say US credit markets, they're incredibly large, they're global. You made a point the last time we spoke that the constituent buyer base is something like 30% in terms of foreign demand.
turns.zh: 所以你提出了一个供给会非常多的论断，但很明显——我们就说美国信用市场吧——它极其庞大，而且是全球性的。你上次来节目时讲过一个点：买家构成里海外需求大约占到 30%。

turns.en: That's right. Walk us through that calculus, how they think about all in yields, I believe you described it that way. And there is at least some discussion, people throw the Scott Besant quasi intervention on the yen into the fear that Japanese capital could be repatriated if Japanese interest rates go up too much.
turns.zh: 没错。给我们讲讲这笔账——他们是怎么考虑到期收益率（all-in yields）的，我记得你是这么表述的。眼下至少也有些讨论：有人把 Scott Bessent 那次对日元的准干预，跟如果日本利率升得太多、日本资本可能回流本土的担忧联系在一起。

turns.en: How should we think about the reaction function of that large foreign buyer base? So the Federal Reserve data shows us that 29% of the US corporate bond market is owned by foreign investors and that figure may even be understated, given that some of that flow may route towards domestic asset managers, but working with the 30% that's sizable in its own, so it underscores why the foreign appetite for US dollar credit receives consistent attention.
turns.zh: 我们该怎么看这一庞大海外买家群体的反应函数？美联储（Federal Reserve）数据显示，美国公司债市场里 29% 为外国投资者持有，这个数字甚至可能被低估，因为其中一些资金流向可能经由国内资产管理人；但就按 30% 来说，它本身已经相当可观，也凸显了为什么海外对美元信用的胃口一直备受关注。

turns.en: The rise in global bond yields as you correctly noted has reignited this conversation around the potential for foreign investors' appetite for US credit to wane.
turns.zh: 正如你恰当指出的，全球债券收益率的上升，重新点燃了海外投资者对美国信用兴趣可能减弱的讨论。

turns.en: But if you look at the tick data, so this is from the Treasury, that's one of the best data sources that exists for tracking foreign flows, what you see is that for the first half of 2026, foreign investors purchased 251 billion on net of US corporate credit, which puts 2026 on pace to exceed the full year record, which was set in 2025.
turns.zh: 但如果你看逐笔交易数据（tick data），也就是财政部数据——这是追踪海外资金流最好的来源之一——你会发现：2026 年上半年，外国投资者净买入 2510 亿美元美国公司信用，这让 2026 年全年有望超过 2025 年创下的全年纪录。

turns.en: And taking a big step back, what is so notable about the foreign flows is actually they've remained robust through the past few years, despite a range of factors that on paper could have argued for foreign demand to slow, the strength of the US dollar, the fluctuation in the cost of US dollar hedging, just to name a few.
turns.zh: 再退一大步看，海外资金流真正值得注意的一点，是过去几年它们一直保持稳健，尽管纸面上有一系列因素本可以让海外需求放缓，比如美元走强、美元对冲成本的起伏，仅举几例。

turns.en: What we have outlined is that we think that there's a floor under foreign demand for a few reasons. The most important is that we believe the key driver of foreign demand for US dollar credit are really just the basic fundamentals, macroeconomic growth, fundamental strength of corporate credit, and then importantly, the size of the market, where there are actually very few options for foreign investors who are looking
turns.zh: 我们给出的判断是：海外需求存在一个下限，原因有几条。最重要的是，我们相信海外对美元信用需求的关键驱动，其实就是最基本的那些——宏观经济增长、公司信用的基本面强度，以及非常重要的市场规模——因为对于那些想要

turns.en: to take corporate credit risk to allocate outside of the US. Europe is the next sizable market, but it's less than half the size than the US is.
turns.zh: 承担公司信用风险、到美国之外去配置的海外投资者来说，实际上选择非常少。欧洲是规模上下一个 sizable 的市场，但不足美国的一半。

turns.en: So for that reason, we do expect that floor to remain in place, and hedging costs in particular are well below the 2022-2023 peaks for European and Japanese investors.
turns.zh: 所以正因为如此，我们确实预期那个下限会继续存在；尤其对欧洲和日本投资者而言，对冲成本都远低于 2022-2023 年的峰值。

turns.en: And so on the margin, that may be a tailwind, but it's not the key driver in our view. On the Japanese investor point, the most notable takeaway that I would reference is actually from the Bank of Japan's Financial Stability Report, which was published earlier this year in April.
turns.zh: 所以在边际上，那或许是一股顺风，但它不是我们眼里的关键驱动。关于日本投资者这一点，我觉得最值得引用的结论，其实来自日本央行（Bank of Japan）今年早些时候、4 月发布的金融稳定报告。

turns.en: And in it, the piece outlined that for Japanese banks, as it relates to foreign investments, they actually had an increased appetite for areas like collateralized loan obligations and alternative assets, ways that they can pick up additional carry and income and diversification, and they mentioned private equity in particular, and actually less demand for IG and high-yield corporate bonds.
turns.zh: 报告里指出：就日本银行的海外投资而言，它们实际上对担保贷款凭证（collateralized loan obligations，CLO）和另类资产的兴趣在上升——这些都是它们获取额外 carry、收入和分散化的方式，报告特别提到私募股权（private equity），而对 IG 与高收益公司债的需求反而更低。

turns.en: So on the margin, there could be some slowing from certain cohorts of the market, but again, the tick data shows us actually the bulk of the foreign flows, more than half are from Europe.
turns.zh: 所以在边际上，某些市场群体或许会有些放缓，但再一次，逐笔交易数据显示，海外资金流里大部分——超过一半——来自欧洲。

turns.en: And again, I think just given the competing alternatives are few and far between as it relates to corporate credit, we do think that the foreign investor appetite for US domiciled credit will remain robust.
turns.zh: 再强调一次，我觉得正因为在公司信用上可竞争的替代选择少之又少，我们确实认为海外投资者对美国本土信用的胃口会保持稳健。

turns.en: When you step back and you just look at the overall big picture environment for spreads, you're being compensated for bearing, some maybe liquidity risk, some default risk, and of course, maybe macro unknowns.
turns.zh: 当你退后一步，只看利差所处的整体大环境，你获得的补偿，对应的是承担某种流动性风险、某种违约风险，当然还有某种宏观上的未知。

turns.en: You've got to look around corners as a credit investor, because as we were saying, the best you could do is get your money back, so we're always worried.
turns.zh: 作为信用投资者，你必须往前多看几个弯，因为就像我们说的，最好的结果不过是拿回本金，所以我们一直在担心。

turns.en: What in your conversations with institutional clients comes up most consistently as, hey, these are on my mind for potential unwelcome events?
turns.zh: 在你跟机构客户的对话里，最反复出现、被当作放在心上、可能带来不受欢迎事件的是些什么？

turns.en: What are the things that come up in the conversations? I think as a strategist, it's always very uncomfortable to justify so much of the performance on technical factors.
turns.zh: 那些对话里浮现的是些什么？我觉得作为策略师，把这么多表现都归因于技术面因素，总让人很不踏实。

turns.en: Yeah, that is essentially where we are in 2026, is that we're looking at the resilient level of spreads, and we're attributing it in large part to some technical factors, including yield-based demand.
turns.zh: 是的，这基本上就是 2026 年我们所处的位置——我们看到利差如此有韧性，并在很大程度上把它归因于一些技术面因素，包括收益率导向的需求。

turns.en: And so that is the risk that I see. I mentioned it at the start, but I am very focused on risks around that theme. So that could mean the yield-based demand becomes less convicted in the US credit market because of an increase in rates vol.
turns.zh: 所以我看到的就是这个风险。我开头提到过，我非常关注围绕这个主题的风险。也就是说，因为利率波动（rates vol）上升，收益率导向的需求对美国信用市场的信心可能减弱。

turns.en: It could also mean, while not the base case of our economists, if we have a sharp downturn in growth, you would have a scenario where spreads would be wider and presumably yields would fall.
turns.zh: 也可能是——虽然不是我们经济学家的基准情形——如果增长急跌，你会看到一个利差走阔、而收益率大概会下降的场景。

turns.en: And so while that may provide some near-term support, hopefully for total returns through a retracement in yields, on the go forward, that could provide a less compelling yield backdrop for corporate credit.
turns.zh: 所以虽然那可能通过收益率回撤、在短期内为总回报提供一些支撑，但往前看，那可能给公司信用提供一个不那么有吸引力的收益率背景。

turns.en: So it really does, I think, provide some sort of vulnerability to the credit market that the yield-based backdrop has been such a powerful technical tailwind.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得，收益率背景作为技术面顺风实在太强，这确实给信用市场带来某种脆弱性。

turns.en: And if that unwinds, that would leave the risks to spreads as wider. And so that's definitely on our radar. It's incredibly difficult to time that.
turns.zh: 一旦这股顺风消退，利差的风险就会偏向更宽。这当然在我们的雷达上，但要择时极其困难。

turns.en: We often get asked, is there a level of yields that becomes detrimental for corporate credit? And I really push back on pinpointing a value because I think it's far more about what are the drivers of the backup in yields and what is the velocity of that?
turns.zh: 我们常被问：有没有一个收益率水平会对公司信用造成伤害？我真的不太愿意给出一个具体点位，因为我认为更重要的，其实是推动收益率上行的驱动因素是什么、以及上行的速度有多快。

turns.en: So if nominal growth is holding in well and that's what's pushing up US Treasury yields, that is a backdrop that credit can digest. And presumably that would also insulate the negative headwind to fundamentals if growth is resilient.
turns.zh: 所以，如果名义增长保持稳固，并且正是它在推高美国国债收益率，那这种背景是信用可以消化的；而且如果增长有韧性，那大概也会隔离掉对基本面的负面逆风。

turns.en: By contrast, if rates are backing up for more negative reasons, not because of resilient growth, but otherwise, maybe it's fiscal concerns, for example, then that would be a backdrop that credit would not digest as easily.
turns.zh: 相反，如果利率上行是出于更负面的原因——不是因为韧性的增长，而是别的，比如财政担忧——那这种背景信用就没那么容易消化。

turns.en: And so that is what we are focused on for sure. And then just like we are monitoring in private credit, we are also monitoring just the overall economic backdrop.
turns.zh: 所以这确实是我们专注的地方。此外，就像我们在私人信贷里做监测一样，我们也在监测整体经济背景。

turns.en: And at the end of the day, these are risk assets and it is the resilient level of growth that is probably most important for the outlook for corporate profitability.
turns.zh: 说到底，这些是风险资产，而对信用前景最重要的，大概是增长的韧性——因为它关系到公司盈利的前景。

turns.en: Of course, the AI theme is a very large factor in that. But I think it's less about competition for capital, less about those sorts of factors and just more about episodic digestion of supply and then keeping an eye on the potential tipping point of some of these technical tailwinds to potentially be less supportive or even morph into technical headwinds in the future.
turns.zh: 当然，AI 主题在其中是一个非常大的因素。但我想，问题更少在于资本竞争之类，更少在于那类因素，而更多在于供给的间歇性消化，然后要盯着这些技术面顺风可能到达的临界点——未来它们可能变得不那么支撑，甚至演变成技术面逆风。

turns.en: I'm remembering back, I want to say it's maybe 2021. It peaked, it seemed like the duration of the index products back then just went sky high because rates were so low.
turns.zh: 我回想起来，应该是大概 2021 年。见顶的时候，指数产品的久期好像一下子就飙得很高，因为利率实在太低了。

turns.en: Of course, that's changed, but the bond market, i.e. the risk-free market, certainly becomes more of a topic of conversation these days. Are the conversations sometimes centering around, look, I'm clipping a coupon from a spread standpoint, but I do have this base asset called US Treasuries that's moving around a little bit and hard to predict.
turns.zh: 当然现在情况变了，但债券市场——也就是无风险市场——如今确实更成了大家谈论的话题。这些讨论里，是不是有时候会围绕这个：你看，从利差角度我拿到了一笔票息，但我这个叫美国国债的基础资产价格上窜下跳、难以预测？

turns.en: Give us a sense as to how much of the treasury component is a part of the conversation on the overall risk that your credit investor clients are taking.
turns.zh: 给我们一个感觉：在你的信用投资者客户所承担的整体风险里，国债成分在多大程度上成了讨论的一部分？

turns.en: It's a very large component for the very primary reason that if you look at all-in-yields, both across US IG and European IG, what you see is that anywhere from 15 to 20% of the all-in-yield only is attributed to the credit spread and the rest of it is attributed to the risk-free rate.
turns.zh: 这是一个非常大的组成部分，最根本的原因是：如果你看美国 IG 和欧洲 IG 的到期收益率（all-in yields），你会发现只有大约 15% 到 20% 归因于信用利差，其余都归因于无风险利率。

turns.en: So as an IG investor in particular, what you have found is that IG is in many ways resembling a rate's product, both in terms of thinking about the overall contribution of your all-in-yield, but then also the duration exposure, as you mentioned.
turns.zh: 所以作为 IG 投资者，你会发现 IG 在很多方面越来越像一个利率产品——不管是考虑到期收益率的整体来源构成，还是你之前提到的久期敞口。

turns.en: So it's definitely a more prominent consideration than it was in the period, say, from 2010 to 2021 when the credit spread represented a much larger share of the overall all-in-yield.
turns.zh: 所以它显然比 2010 到 2021 年那段时期更值得关注——那时候信用利差占整体到期收益率的份额要大得多。

turns.en: That being said, I think investors are appropriately almost reconsidering how they think about relative value and credit. And it goes back to what we mentioned at the start, that the periods of spread widening have been episodic, they've been short-lived, and you've really had to act quickly.
turns.zh: 话虽如此，我觉得投资者几乎正在恰当地重新审视他们思考相对价值与信用的方式。这也回到我们开头讲的：利差走阔的窗口是一波一波、转瞬即逝的，你真的必须动作很快。

turns.en: And so what I sense increasingly from investor conversations is that even investors that hadn't historically considered themselves yield-based investors are just increasingly acknowledging the attractiveness of the all-in-yield backdrop and how that is influencing the level of spreads.
turns.zh: 所以我从投资者对话里越来越感觉到的是，甚至一些历来不把自己看作收益率导向投资者的人，也越来越承认这个到期收益率背景有多有吸引力，以及它如何影响利差水平。

turns.en: Again, speaking to the importance of that technical and almost reevaluating what is an acceptable level of spreads given the fundamental shifts under the surface in the credit market, which we actually have seen move pretty meaningfully since the financial crisis and the overall economic backdrop.
turns.zh: 这也说明了那项技术面因素的重要性，以及近乎在重新评估——鉴于信用市场表层之下的基本面格局已经发生很大变化，实际上自金融危机以来整体经济和宏观背景都有不小变化——什么才是可接受的利差水平。

turns.en: So definitely a focus, but I think one that investors are just increasingly having to internalize and kind of move forward realizing that there's, in many cases, an opportunity cost to being too defensive in this market.
turns.zh: 所以这确实是一个关注焦点，但我认为投资者越来越需要把它内化，往前看，意识到在很多情况下，在这个市场里过度防御是有机会成本的。

turns.en: And that's part of the reason why, even despite a record forecast for issuance this year and continued next year, we're only baking in modest widening in our spread forecast because we're taking all of these factors on board and acknowledging that there are a lot of anchors keeping spreads resilient, albeit the risks are skewed towards more widening, as I noted at the start.
turns.zh: 这也是原因之一：即便今年发行量预估创纪录、明年还会继续，我们在利差预测里也只反映温和走阔，因为我们把这些因素都纳入考量，也承认有很多锚在维持利差韧性，尽管如我开头所说，风险偏向更宽一点。

turns.en: So take us through some of your thinking on the high yield space. Folks like me trade options on the HYG and it almost never moves the HYG itself.
turns.zh: 那请给我们讲讲你在高收益领域的一些想法。像我这样的人交易 HYG 的期权，而 HYG 本身几乎不动。

turns.en: Some part of that I often hear is just a function of the migration higher in credit quality in high yield. And at least I understand it to be almost two indices in one.
turns.zh: 我常听到的一种解释是，那部分是高收益内部信用质量整体向上迁移的结果。至少我理解，高收益差不多是两个指数合成一个。

turns.en: You mentioned the triple C component as dicey and that's kind of often its own category, but the other parts of the high yield sector seem to be up in quality.
turns.zh: 你提到 CCC 那一档比较微妙，那常常自成一个类别，但高收益板块的其余部分似乎在质量上是上移的。

turns.en: Is that correct? And how do you think about finding value in the high yield sector? I think that's a fair characterization. And I actually think what you've seen across both IG and high yield corporate credit markets is that the barriers to entry to enter the syndicated credit market as an issuer have just grown.
turns.zh: 是这样吗？你怎么看在高收益板块里寻找价值？我觉得这个描述相当到位。我实际上认为，你在 IG 和高收益这两个公司信用市场里看到的，是作为发行人进入银团信贷市场的门槛在不断抬高。

turns.en: And we've run these stats as of a couple of weeks ago, but the average new issue size in USIG was comfortably above 1.5 billion so far this year.
turns.zh: 我们两周前跑了一遍这些统计：今年到目前为止，美国 IG 新发行的平均规模已经稳稳超过 15 亿美元。

turns.en: And the average new issue size in the high yield bond market has been around 900 million in 2026. And actually in the several hundred million dollar range for the past few years, keep in mind that's one deal that's not even a capital structure.
turns.zh: 而高收益债市场里，2026 年新发行的平均规模在 9 亿美元左右——过去几年其实处在数亿美元区间。请记住，那只是一笔交易，甚至还不是一整套资本结构。

turns.en: So for a firm that's looking for incremental capital, small size amounts of financing, what you're increasingly seeing is that they're not coming to the high yield bond market for that because even if they're technically index eligible, you run the risk of being thinly traded, poorly held, and it's just not a great outcome for either the investor or the issuer.
turns.zh: 所以对于需要增量资金、只需要小额融资的公司来说，你会越来越看到它们不再到高收益债市场来拿钱，因为即便它们在技术上可以纳入指数，你的债也容易被交易稀薄、持有人寡少，对投资者和发行人都不算好结果。

turns.en: Of course, there's the growth of private credit and syndicated leverage loans. I push back on this narrative that a lot of the more vulnerable issuers have gone to the private credit market.
turns.zh: 当然，还有私人信贷和银团杠杆贷款的成长。对于很多更脆弱的发行人已经跑到私人信贷市场这个说法，我是有所保留的。

turns.en: I don't think that's the whole story, but I do think that it serves an important financing avenue channel for smaller issuers that just need incremental financing or maybe they need a more bespoke solution because they're earlier in their growth journey and they're finding that in the private market.
turns.zh: 我不认为这是全部真相，但我确实认为，对那些只需要增量融资、或因为仍处在更早期成长阶段而需要更定制方案的较小发行人，它是一条重要的融资渠道——它们在私募市场里找到了这种方案。

turns.en: And so that's contributed to this mixed shift that you've seen where the companies that are accessing the high yield bond market, they're just larger, they're more diverse, they're more liquid.
turns.zh: 所以这促成了你所看到的这种混合变化：进入高收益债市场的公司，就是更大、更多元、更具流动性的。

turns.en: Of course, you've had increased fluidity across IG and high yield as well since the pandemic. And I remember very distinctly in the height of the pandemic when we were worried about the high yield market's ability to absorb 200 billion plus of fallen angels from IG.
turns.zh: 当然，疫情以来 IG 与高收益之间的流动性也更强了。我非常清楚地记得，在疫情高峰时，我们曾担心高收益市场有没有能力消化来自 IG 的超过 2000 亿美元堕落天使（fallen angels）。

turns.en: And what we found is actually the high yield market was more than capable of doing that. And in many instances, that was far less disruptive than I think a lot of us expected.
turns.zh: 结果我们发现，高收益市场其实完全有能力做到这一点，而且很多情况下，其冲击远比我们很多人预期的要小。

turns.en: So the high yield bond market has been very institutionalized and I would say there's a lot more fluidity across IG, especially when you think about that double B, triple B, overlap in terms of relative value and borrowers moving back and forth.
turns.zh: 所以高收益债市场已经非常机构化。我会说 IG 和高收益之间的流动性更强了，尤其是当你想到 BB、BBB 交界那一块，在相对价值上、在借款人来回去上的互通。

turns.en: And where you have the more dicey firms are either in high yield where they just are in that left tail, as I described, that triple C, the lagging part of the market, where not all triple C's are like that, but they're more likely to be in that camp.
turns.zh: 至于更微妙的公司，要么就在高收益里落在我所说的那个左尾——就是 CCC 那一批滞后于市场的部分，并非所有 CCC 都如此，但它们更可能属于这一类。

turns.en: Or in, again, certain pockets of loans and private credit, but more isolated in terms of the really small borrowers. So for sure it has shifted, and I think it's largely a function of some changes in market structure and the evolution of the private credit market in particular as this third viable financing channel in addition to the syndicated credit markets and in addition to bank lending that have scooped up a wide range of borrowers
turns.zh: 要么，再说一次，就在贷款和私人信贷的某些角落里，但更集中于那些真正小的借款人。所以确实是变了，我认为这在很大程度上是市场结构变化、以及私人信贷市场演化——它作为第三条可行的融资渠道，在银团信贷市场和银行贷款之外，把一大批借款人揽入怀中——

turns.en: that are either smaller or earlier in their growth journeys that would have otherwise accessed the high yield bond market. As you were talking about the pandemic, I can't help but think about maybe 2021 and the aftermath, a tremendous amount of refinancing at low rates.
turns.zh: 的结果，它们要么更小、要么处在成长更早期，否则本会进入高收益债市场。你讲疫情那段，让我想到大概 2021 年及其后，那一大批在低利率下的再融资。

turns.en: If you're doom-scrolling on Twitter, you're going to come across inevitably the maturity wall chart. I'm guessing you don't really think that there's much to that given your view on a supply demand, but tell us about the need to refinance stuff that's coming due.
turns.zh: 如果你在 Twitter 上刷到停不下来，你一定会碰到那张到期墙（maturity wall）图表。我猜，按照你对供需的看法，你并不觉得那有多要紧，但请讲讲那些即将到期的债务需要再融资的情况。

turns.en: You're right in that we don't put a ton of weight on maturity walls in every market backdrop, but we are focused on the software maturity wall in 2028 and 2029.
turns.zh: 你说得对，我们不会在任何一种市场背景下把太多权重放在到期墙上，但我们确实关注 2028 和 2029 年软件板块的到期墙。

turns.en: I think in general, you're right, the IG market has been refinancing low rate debt for a while now. It's not as though the COVID era debt was all five years and is only coming up now.
turns.zh: 我觉得总体来说，你是对的：IG 市场已经再融资低利率债务有一段时间了，并不是说新冠时期的债务全是 5 年期、现在才刚到期。

turns.en: We've been dealing with that for a while. You can see that in the average index coupon drifting higher across IG and high yield, recognizing that as companies refinanced into a higher rates backdrop, they were just incurring that higher cost of debt.
turns.zh: 我们处理这个问题已经有一段时间了。从指数平均票息在 IG 与高收益里都在往上漂就能看出来——因为当公司把债务再融到更高利率背景时，它们就是承受了更高的债务成本。

turns.en: Obviously, that's more of a fixed rate phenomenon. Floating rate borrowers had been dealing with that since the start of the Fed and ECB rate hiking cycles a couple of years ago.
turns.zh: 显然，这更多是固定利率的现象。浮动利率借款人则从几年前美联储和欧洲央行（ECB）加息周期一开始，就已经在处理同样的事。

turns.en: I don't think it's detrimental enough to, for example, cause a new peak in the default cycle. We did note recently in our work, however, that we have seen some incremental improvement on interest coverage, but that's probably going to be short-lived because, again, you're going to be refinancing into a global bond yield backup.
turns.zh: 我不认为它严重到会，比如，让违约周期出现一个新的顶峰。不过我们最近的研究确实注意到，我们看到利息保障有一些边际改善，但那大概会很短暂，因为再一次，你再融资的时候正好赶上全球债券收益率往上走。

turns.en: And then, of course, we had a hike from the Fed recently. So we're back into this trend of higher base rates, not lower base rates, and that will probably stem some of the improvement that we've seen for floating rate borrowers.
turns.zh: 然后，当然，美联储最近加息了。所以我们又回到基准利率走高、而不是走低这一趋势，这大概会遏制我们看到的一些浮动利率借款人的改善。

turns.en: Where I do think it is probably worth monitoring is in the software exposure, like I mentioned. That's going to be relevant for both broadly syndicated loans and in private credit.
turns.zh: 我确实认为值得监测的地方，就是我前面提到的软件敞口。这在广泛银团贷款（broadly syndicated loans）和私人信贷里都相关。

turns.en: And I think it's just the disruption to the legacy software business model narrative as it relates to AI. It's just difficult to disprove. We just don't know what the disruption will be.
turns.zh: 我觉得，关于 AI 对传统软件商业模式冲击的那个叙事，就是很难被证伪——我们并不知道冲击会是什么。

turns.en: We feel very confident that it will be nuanced, that we shouldn't paint all of the software firms with one broad brush. Our equity colleagues have published a significant amount of great work on the differences in these business models, the differences in the moats, and the customer relationships, and the ownership of data.
turns.zh: 我们非常有信心的是，冲击会是细分的，我们不该用一把大刷子把所有软件公司刷在一起。我们的股票同事发布了大量很好的研究，谈这些商业模式之间的差异、护城河（moats）的差异、客户关系，以及数据的所有权。

turns.en: So all of that, I think, lays the groundwork for credit selection. But at the very minimum, we think that that overhang will persist until we see more consistent evidence of refinancings coming through that market.
turns.zh: 所以我认为，这些为信用挑选打下了基础。但最起码，我们认为那层阴云会持续存在，直到我们在这个市场里看到更多、更一致的再融资通过案例。

turns.en: The ones that we've seen have gone well. So I think that's important to acknowledge that the 2028 and 2029 exposures in loans and private credit weren't monitoring.
turns.zh: 我们看到的再融资进行得都不错。所以我觉得有一点值得指出：贷款和私人信贷里 2028、2029 年的敞口，是我们一直在监测的。

turns.en: And we think more of that will be coming over the next, call it, six to 12 months as companies get ahead of that. Well, let's finish with some of your thoughts on diversification and portfolio construction.
turns.zh: 我们预计在未来——姑且说——六到十二个月里，随着公司提前处理，会有更多这样的再融资到来。那我们就用一些你在分散化和组合构建上的想法来收尾吧。

turns.en: On the equity side, the market has magically diversified itself. The correlation of stocks is considerably lower than the correlation of the stock market to the bond market.
turns.zh: 在股票这边，市场已经神奇地自我分散化了。个股之间的相关性，远低于股票市场与债券市场之间的相关性。

turns.en: The risk on risk off between the S&P and rates is more, they're kind of attached at the hip relative to the negative correlation we used to see, but stocks themselves are vastly uncorrelated.
turns.zh: 标普与利率之间的 risk-on risk-off 更有点像形影不离，不像过去那种负相关；但股票彼此之间却是高度不相关的。

turns.en: And one of the risks, I think, is people think they're more diversified than they turn out to be. And so I tend to try to spend a lot of time trying to find pockets of crowdedness and really pushing for assets that can serve as diversifiers, that can buffer returns when other parts of the portfolio do poorly.
turns.zh: 我觉得一个风险是，人们以为自己比实际上更分散。所以我通常会花很多时间去找那些拥挤的角落，并极力推动配置那些能起到分散化作用的资产——在组合其他部分表现不佳时能给回报做缓冲。

turns.en: You'd mentioned pharma and healthcare. I thought that was super interesting. Just talk a little bit more about your thoughts on portfolio construction and this unique time when we're seeing this just massive issue in cycle from the hyperscalers.
turns.zh: 你提到过制药和医疗健康，我觉得特别有意思。请再多讲讲你在组合构建上的想法，以及眼下这个由超大规模云服务商掀起的巨大发行周期的独特时刻。

turns.en: I would highlight two things as it relates to this. One is going back to what we mentioned earlier, which is for all of the focus on the capital needs and the financing needs of the hyperscalers, this is a much broader theme in corporate credit.
turns.zh: 关于这一点我会强调两条。第一，回到我们之前说的：尽管大家都在关注超大规模云服务商的资本需求和融资需求，但这一主题在公司信用里其实要宽得多。

turns.en: And so it's not just about a handful of names issuing into the market, but it's a wide range of issuers accessing financing markets. And so keeping track of that and really broadening your view of what is AI related, I think will be increasingly important as the years progress, especially as these issuers become larger percentages of the broader market.
turns.zh: 所以这不是只有几个名字在发行，而是一大批发行人进入融资市场。因此，跟踪好这一点，并真正拓宽你对什么算 AI 相关的视野，我认为随着年份推移会越来越重要，尤其当这些发行人占整个更大市场的比重不断上升时。

turns.en: The second point that I would note as it relates to portfolio construction is actually something that our colleagues in portfolio strategy research have noted for a while now, which is the increasing value of including real assets in your portfolio.
turns.zh: 第二点，关于组合构建，其实是我们的组合策略研究（portfolio strategy research）同事已经指出了一段时间的：把实物资产（real assets）纳入组合的价值在上升。

turns.en: And I think that's something that has been more achievable post financial crisis as the private markets have grown. But when you think about uncorrelated exposures, assets with inflation pass through or inflation protection, so that could be commodities or infrastructure or real estate, that is where I think the evolution of portfolio construction has really evolved and less from this 60, 40 portfolio,
turns.zh: 我觉得这在金融危机之后随着私募市场成长变得更可行了。当你想到不相关的敞口、带通胀传导或通胀保护的资产——那可以是大宗商品、基础设施或房地产——我认为那才是组合构建真正演化所在，而越来越少停留在那种 60/40 组合，

turns.en: but more towards 50, 30, 20 as some call it or this broader exposure of assets. And that I think is probably a trend that is here to stay irrespective of the AI related theme as well.
turns.zh: 而是更多走向所谓 50/30/20，或者更宽的一类资产配置。我认为这一趋势大概会长期持续，无论 AI 相关主题如何。

turns.en: Well, Amanda, it was a pleasure to host this conversation. I'm really glad you took me up on the offer to come back. And I think our listeners are gonna learn a lot about corporate credit from this discussion.
turns.zh: 好，Amanda，非常荣幸主持这场对话。我很高兴你接受了我请你回来的邀请，我相信我们的听众会在这场讨论里学到很多公司信用的东西。

turns.en: So thank you. Thank you so much for having me, Dean. It was great to be back. Thank you. Absolutely. You've been listening to the Alpha Exchange.
turns.zh: 所以谢谢。非常谢谢你邀请我，Dean，很高兴回来。谢谢你。当然。你刚才收听的是 Alpha Exchange。

turns.en: If you've enjoyed the show, please do tell a friend. And before we leave, I wanted to invite you to drop us some feedback. As we aim to utilize these conversations to contribute to the investment community's understanding of risk, your input is valuable and provides direction on where we should focus.
turns.zh: 如果你喜欢这个节目，请务必告诉一位朋友。在我们道别之前，我想邀请你给我留一些反馈。由于我们致力于通过这些对话为投资界理解风险做出贡献，你的意见很有价值，也为我们应该把重点放在哪里提供方向。

turns.en: Please email us at feedback at alphaexchangepodcast.com. Thanks again and catch you next time.
turns.zh: 请发邮件到 feedback@alphaexchangepodcast.com 给我们。再次感谢，我们下次再见。
